XRP on Track to Post Worst ETF Month Ever

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (241 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The XRP ETF market might be bracing to close a record-breaking month of outflows as demand for the XRP-based investment product has remained on hold all through the month.
  • This comes as the prolonged and intense market volatility has extended to the ETF ecosystem, causing institutional investors to withdraw their capital.
  • With November just about three weeks gone, the latest data from SoSoValue shows that XRP ETFs have already recorded a total of $30.76 million in net outflows this November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The XRP ETF market might be bracing to close a record-breaking month of outflows as demand for the XRP-based investment product has remained on hold all through the month.

This comes as the prolonged and intense market volatility has extended to the ETF ecosystem, causing institutional investors to withdraw their capital.

With November just about three weeks gone, the latest data from SoSoValue shows that XRP ETFs have already recorded a total of $30.76 million in net outflows this November.

Previous ETF data reveals that March remains the only month in which spot XRP ETFs have recorded net outflows since their launch.

While it still stands as the record outflow month for XRP ETFs, investors withdrew about $31.16 million from the funds during that month.

This means that the persistent withdrawals seen this month have brought the November outflow dangerously close to its previous monthly record seen in March.

Apparently, the spot XRP ETFs are on track to close November as their worst-performing month since launch, with just about $1 million left to hit the record.

Further data also highlights that the spot XRP ETFs have yet to record a single day of net inflows throughout November, as the persistent price decline has caused investors to slow down their purchases.

As such, the influx of fresh capital into the spot XRP ETF market has remained on hold amid growing market uncertainty and a shift in investor sentiment.

Breaking: Hyundai is shaking up its 2027 electric vehicle lineup: Here’s what’s changing

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (703 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyundai’s US electric vehicle lineup will look a bit different in 2027, including the new IONIQ 6 N, a new range-topping IONIQ 9 trim, and a handful of minor updates to the IONIQ 5.
  • Hyundai declared its 2027 model-year changes on Wednesday, including the fresh IONIQ 6 N and a few slight changes to the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.
  • While Hyundai discontinued the standard IONIQ 6, it added the high-performance IONIQ 6 N for the 2027 lineup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai’s US electric vehicle lineup will look a bit different in 2027, including the new IONIQ 6 N, a new range-topping IONIQ 9 trim, and a handful of minor updates to the IONIQ 5.

Hyundai declared its 2027 model-year changes on Wednesday, including the fresh IONIQ 6 N and a few slight changes to the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.

While Hyundai discontinued the standard IONIQ 6, it added the high-performance IONIQ 6 N for the 2027 lineup.

The IONIQ 6 N is Hyundai’s second performance EV, following the IONIQ 5 N. Powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, the electric sports car delivers a combined 641 hp and 568 lb-ft of torque.

Hyundai said the IONIQ 6 N can sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 3.2 seconds, beating the IONIQ 5 N at 3.25 seconds.

Like the IONIQ 5 N, it also includes fun added features, like N e-Shift and an N Active Sound+ system that simulates the sounds and sensations of a traditional gas-powered sports car with an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission.

In a recent development, it uses an 84 kWh battery that provides up to 245 miles of pure electric driving range. Thanks to its 800V ultra-fast charging architecture, the IONIQ 6 N can charge from 10% to 80% in about 18 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Like Hyundai’s other electric vehicles, it comes standard with a native NACS charging port and a CCS adapter.

The 2027 IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are mostly carryover models with a few minor changes, while the IONIQ 5 N remains the same as the 2026 model year.

Changes to the IONIQ 5 for the 2027 model year include roof rails, which are now available on the SEL trim and above; previously, they were only available on the XRT and Limited trims.

Hyundai HomeLink will be available exclusively on the Limited trim, rather than SEL and above, in the current 2026 model year, while the Cargo Cover will be offered as an Accessory only.

Regarding color options, the Gravity Gold Matte and Sage Silver Matte will no longer be available for the 2027 IONIQ 5.

The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250, making it one of the most affordable EVs in the US.

According to recent reports, that’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. The extended-range SE RWD model is $2,500 more, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row SUV also received a handful of updates. The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 9 will be available with a newly introduced Calligraphy Black Ink trim, while the Calligraphy Design will no longer be offered.

Sources indicate that the 2027 IONIQ 9 Calligraphy and Calligraphy Black Ink trims gain a Virtual Gear Shift and heated third-row seats. All variants also gain a Tailgate Emergency Lamp.

It has been revealed that on the one hand... the Ioniq5 is due for an patch. On the other... I still absolutely love the way it looks, and notice just about every one I pass on the road.

In a recent development, hyundai has yet to announce prices for the 2027 model. The base 2026 IONIQ 9 S starts at $58,995 and offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 335 miles.

The previous top-spec Performance Calligraphy Design AWD started at $76,490, so you can expect the new Calligraphy Black Ink to be around the same, if not even more.

Bitcoin’s price hits ‘bottom territory’ after BTC falls below $60K — What next?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (408 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less than half of all Bitcoin [BTC] is green right now, and that’s not a good look.
  • As of 18th November, those are the numbers.
  • Every major BTC bottom since 2015 has happened with less than half the supply in the green.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than half of all Bitcoin [BTC] is green right now, and that’s not a good look. In fact, as it turns out, we may not see light anytime soon.

As of 18th November, those are the numbers. At least according to the Rand Group.

Every major BTC bottom since 2015 has happened with less than half the supply in the green. In August 2025, that figure was 35.7%. It hit 39.8% in December 2018, 42.5% in March 2020, and 44.8% in November 2022.

This June, it was as low as 46.9%.

It has been revealed that each low has come in a little higher than the one before. Holders are giving up less ground with every cycle. The argument is that the best opportunities show up when most holders are underwater, not when everyone’s celebrating.

Hence, the question: Does that mean the bottom is in? No, But Bitcoin is in a zone where that has mattered before.

… might be tech stocks and rates, according to QCP Capital.

Industry observers note that not everyone’s ready to call it a bottom, yet. In fact, the digital asset partner thinks Bitcoin’s problem is about money getting tight everywhere.

Industry observers note that earlier this cycle, ETF buying, corporate treasuries, and hopes of rate cuts did a good job of soaking up selling. That support will crack when stocks drop across the board.

So, what would it take to turn things around?

Its report cited three things, namely,.

…recovery will likely require stabilisation in technology equities, reduced volatility in rates and evidence that institutional flows are returning.

Until then, any bounce driven by shorts closing out could fizzle fast. The Fed could also be another weight on BTC’s back.

At the time of writing, the charts weren’t really comforting either. BTC was trading at $58,681, down 5.2% over the last 24 hours. Just a couple of weeks ago, it was trading above $80K.

The RSI was knee deep in oversold territory, its lowest reading in months. Sellers have been running out fuel, but oversold conditions can stay as such for a while.

The ADX was 43.8 and still rising. So, the downtrend seemed to be getting stronger. Especially since buyers didn’t look like they were going to turn up.

In a recent development, this is a bottom range that we know. However, until the selling pressure slows down, calling it the floor would be a gamble.

Sources indicate that dogecoin co-founder Billy Markus, known on X as Shibetoshi Nakamoto, reacted to the recent market decline, which saw over $2.56 billion in liquidations. He hinted at weak demand as a possible reason behind the massive sell-off.

Markus earlier wrote in a post that "Black Friday came early." This came as the broader financial markets dropped, not just crypto: tech stocks, gold, copper, and Asian equities all fell.

Markus’s post garnered attention from the Dogecoin community and the wider crypto community. A Dogecoin community member responded: “Am I retarded for thinking crypto is about to go up?”.

@alphadoge777 well it always goes up and down 🤣 but the market has been looking pretty low demand for awhile now.

"Well, it always goes up and down," Markus remarked, pointing to crypto's inherent volatility and adding that the market had been experiencing "pretty low demand for a while now.".

His comments come as the crypto market continues to crash, highlighting concerns about the lack of buying interest needed to prop up prices.

Markus did not point to a specific catalyst for the decline, but his remarks highlight an important ingredient for a bullish comeback in the market: demand.

It has been revealed that the crypto market selloff deepened on Saturday, with Bitcoin hitting its lowest level since September 2024 and extending a brutal run for risk assets. Dogecoin was trading in the red, down 8.13% in the last 24 hours to $0.528 and down 16% weekly. Dogecoin fell to $0.05 earlier on Saturday, a low not seen since June 2022.

Data from Coinglass at press time show that $2.56 billion was liquidated in crypto positions over the past 24 hours; longs accounted for 89.2% of this total, at $2.28 billion, while short liquidations came in at $276,040.

Analysts pointed to rising real, or inflation-adjusted, U.S. Treasury yields as a key driver of the ongoing sell-off, which extends a bear market that began in October of last year.

Crypto investors are searching for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026. The broader crypto market has dropped since the Clarity Act faced a setback in September.

The National Basketball Association’s latest venture, though, might be its most accessible to date, and it’s one we didn’t really see coming: Amazon Essentials x NBA.

Shop the Amazon Essentials x NBA Collection.

It has been revealed that we also highlighted a couple of pieces for the little ones, including a French Terry Crewneck Sweatshirt and a Soft Fleece Zip-Up Hoodie. All things considered, color us impressed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has confirmed a new batch of Tesla Semi deliveries, with its official Semi account saying today that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are on their way to the city.

In a recent development, it’s a rare data point. Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, and it claims its newly introduced Nevada factory can build 50,000 of them a year.

The post, published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, highlights four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.

Hello Windy CityChicago’s first 50 Semis en route for delivery pic.twitter.com/75kig8yWsb.

Recent findings suggest that but the only 50-truck Semi order tied to Chicago belongs to HMD Trucking. The family-owned carrier was founded in Chicago in 1998, runs more than 650 trucks (almost all diesel), and ordered 50 Semis right after Tesla’s production event in September.

It has been revealed that HMD took its first truck on November 2 and claims it’s the first Tesla Semi registered in Illinois. COO Michael Mahler stated Tesla “has been transparent with us regarding the capabilities of Semi every step of the way.”.

Sources indicate that the tech giant ran a Semi for more than 4,000 miles over the summer and averaged 1.74 kWh per mile, right in line with Tesla’s 1.7 kWh/mile claim. The first trucks will mostly handle local runs around Chicago, and HMD is installing its own chargers there since Tesla’s Megacharger network is still concentrated along the I-5 and I-10 corridors in the West.

It has been revealed that owner Henry Malukas told MotorTrend the deal is worth about $15 million. That’s roughly $300,000 per truck, in line with the ~$290,000 Long Range pricing we reported when the first truck came off the high-volume line and a long way from the $180,000 Tesla advertised in 2017.

Here’s the problem: it’s nearly impossible to tell how many Semis Tesla is actually building.

Tesla launched volume production at its Sparks, Nevada factory on September 24, after pushing the ramp out of 2025. It says the 1.8 million sq ft plant is built for 50,000 trucks a year. But it never gave a ramp schedule, and its quarterly production and delivery reports only count “passenger vehicles sold to customers.” The Semi isn’t in there.

So we’re left with proxies. Tesla says its Semi fleet has over 98% uptime, without saying how substantial that fleet is. Before this year, the largest Semi fleet was PepsiCo’s, at 86 trucks in 2024. California’s truck voucher program received 965 Semi applications between January 2025 and February 2026, which points to real demand but says nothing about output.

The order book is the other clue. Einride ordered 500 Semis in August, WattEV has 370 on order, IMC Logistics wants 50 for California, and the ZET SCALE alliance picked Tesla as main supplier for 2,500 trucks. And now HMD’s 50 are rolling into Chicago, one of the first Semi fleets that will have to deal with a Midwest winter. Wisconsin’s Paper Transport has also been piloting a Semi in the Chicago market since the summer.

None of that adds up to a production rate, but it does look like Tesla is slowly ramping up deliveries.

Tesla keeps the Semi numbers vague on purpose. It’s happy to talk about a 50,000-truck-a-year factory, and it posts hero shots when a batch ships, but it won’t give the one number that shows whether the factory is anywhere close to that.

I think the semi is going to be a big seller but its going to take some time to produce enough of them and for companies to gather enough data. Once the investment is justified, there will be customers and repeat customers. After that, it will only be a matter of time before other electric semi truck manufacturers start popping up with offerings and thats a good thing for everyone.

The 50,000 figure is what makes the Semi look like a real business to investors instead of a niche program that took nine years to get going. Tesla has a long history of quoting capacity long before it reaches it, so we shouldn’t treat “built for 50,000” as anything more than a ceiling.

Sources indicate that our read: Tesla is still far from that 50,000 rate. Fifty trucks for one customer is 0.1% of a year at full capacity, and if Tesla were shipping in large volumes, a single 50-unit batch wouldn’t get its own post. But the ramp has clearly started, the order book is real, and it’s plausible Tesla gets into the thousands by the end of the year.

Good for HMD, too. A 650-truck diesel fleet in a cold market is exactly the kind of customer the Semi has to win. Malukas admitted “we don’t have real numbers yet” on savings, and HMD’s own blog is fairly sober about cost and winter range. Local routes, depot charging and a Chicago winter is the right way to find out. It all sounds plausible for the Tesla Semi.

Breaking: Tesla extends Cybertruck production to late summer 2027 amid fan backlash

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk now indicates Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first unveiled it was killing it.
  • The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it states about Tesla’s future as a company that sells cars to people.
  • On November 6, Musk noted Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas “around the middle of next year” to make room for Cybercab.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk now indicates Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first unveiled it was killing it.

The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it states about Tesla’s future as a company that sells cars to people.

On November 6, Musk noted Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas “around the middle of next year” to make room for Cybercab. On November 9, he wrote the line would shut “in about 8 months” and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.” Now it’s the end of summer.

In order to work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog, production will be extended through the end of summer 2027.

The reasons have moved around just as much. First it was factory space, then “a very limited number of smart, dedicated people,” then the “opportunity cost” of the truck’s complexity. We went through each of them: Tesla is ending the Cybertruck as sales stall at about 10% of proposal, Musk’s demand claim doesn’t survive the numbers, and Musk admitted Tesla doesn’t have the talent to run more than one vehicle program.

And the “backlog” is one Tesla built itself. Before the announcement, the truck was selling at a pace of roughly 30,000 units a year, about 10% of the 250,000 Tesla planned for, on a line with over 125,000 units of installed capacity. Telling people the truck is going away creates a last-call rush. That’s not demand Tesla was missing before.

Tesla also raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% the same day and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. The cheapest Cybertruck you can order is now $92,490, up from $69,990 in early August.

Recent findings suggest that some of the people in that backlog have been waiting a while. Several cheering in Musk’s replies say they’re still waiting on the $59,990 Cybertruck Tesla sold for “10 days only” in February. One asked whether Tesla will prioritize Premium and Cyberbeast orders over theirs. Musk didn’t answer.

The most telling replies weren’t about the truck. Chuck Cook, one of the best-known FSD testers in the Tesla community, quote-tweeted Musk asking him to “change your mind,” adding: “Cybercab won’t haul my bees.”.

Another longtime Tesla supporter, Phil Trubey, asked for “a vehicle roadmap post end of summer 2027,” followed by: “Will Tesla make any other vehicle?”.

Industry observers note that that’s the right question, and Tesla hasn’t revealed a single newly introduced consumer vehicle to answer it. Tesla started 2026 with five consumer vehicle programs: Model S, Model X, Model 3, Model Y, and Cybertruck. It ended Model S and Model X production in the spring, citing “autonomy.” The Cybertruck goes next. By fall 2027, Tesla’s consumer lineup will be the Model 3 and Model Y, two vehicles that debuted in 2017 and 2020.

Tesla’s answer to the affordable car it promised for years was stripped-down “Standard” versions of those same two vehicles. In China, its second-biggest market, Tesla turned Giga Shanghai into an export hub, and domestic retail sales crashed 66% in October to the lowest level in over four years.

Sources indicate that even Unplugged Performance, the biggest Tesla tuner around, offered to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands and pay a license fee. People want this truck built. Tesla doesn’t.

We’ve been warning about this for years, and for years we got called haters for it.

Sources indicate that the pattern has been clear since Tesla swapped its affordable car prepares for Robotaxi in 2024. No newly introduced consumer platform. Model S and X killed “for autonomy.” Cybertruck killed “for Cybercab.” A Roadster pitched as a thruster stunt nine years after its unveiling. Every product decision points away from selling cars to people and toward robotaxis and Optimus, two businesses that don’t generate meaningful revenue today.

I am beginning to suspect that Elon does not always tell the truth.

As long as we have an economic climate that allows massive amounts of money to be made off of speculation as opposed to actual product, future bots and robotaxis have a great deal of value whether they actually become viable or not.

A two-to-three-month extension doesn’t change any of that. It’s a gesture to the loudest part of the fan base, and it happens to let Tesla sell a few thousand more trucks at prices up to 10% higher than last week. Fine. But the people who bought into Tesla’s mission to accelerate the world’s transition to sustainable energy are now realizing that mission was quietly rewritten, and the word “sustainable” didn’t make the cut.

It has been revealed that tesla is becoming a company that sells two aging EVs to fund a bet on autonomy. That might work out for shareholders. We have our doubts, given Tesla is still behind Waymo by every public metric. But it’s a lot less exciting for the people who wanted the next great Tesla car.

The question for fans now: when the Model 3 and Model Y get their own “opportunity cost” post on X, will anyone actually be surprised?

As a result, there has been a decline in the amount of stETH immediately available on exchanges for potential selling.

This comes as Ethereum was trading near $1,753.91 at press time, after a drop of 2.9% in the past 24 hours.

Industry observers note that at the same time, around 836,798 ETH is presently waiting to enter Ethereum’s validator network. Of this, the estimated waiting period currently stands at 14 days and 13 hours, with a processing rate (churn) of 256 ETH per epoch.

Meanwhile, the exit queue presents a different picture wherein around 164,005 ETH is waiting to leave the validator network, with an estimated waiting period of 3 days and 20 hours.

Sources indicate that looking at the broader picture, Ethereum right now has approximately 773,650 active validators, with 44.6 million ETH staked. This represents around 36.5% of Ethereum’s total supply, while the network’s annual percentage rate (APR) stands at 2.42%.

So now, if exchange outflows continue, the entry queue remains elevated, and ETH prices begin stabilizing, these developments could strengthen the argument that investors are positioning themselves for the longer term rather than preparing to sell into market weakness.

Interestingly, all of this coincided with a recent report by AMBCrypto where Ethereum’s staking ratio has reportedly reached an all-time high of 36.3%, with approximately 44.5 million ETH locked in staking, up from 42.1 million in mid-August.

Meanwhile, institutional players such as BitMine and SharpLink continue expanding their staking activities, with BitMine holding 5.22 million staked ETH and earning $121.4 million from staking and validation.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its upcoming full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels.

The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.

After opening preorders at the Beijing Auto Show in April, BYD said the high-end SUV secured over 30,000 preorders in 24 hours. Two weeks later, preorders reached over 100,000.

By the time it went on sale in mid-June, over 150,000 buyers had preordered the Great Tang, marking a latest record for a single BYD model.

While it has been the top-selling pure electric large SUV for two months, with more than 10,000 sold since it hit the market, BYD issued an apology on November 11 for fitting the wrong front and rear wheel rims on some Great Tang models.

The apology comes after several owners complained that the wheels were improperly installed on their vehicles.

BYD said the issue stemmed from a coding error by the wheel mesh assembly supplier, which led to incorrect assembly on some Great Tang vehicles.

The firm said it “immediately” released an investigation and corrected the concern so newly built vehicles will not be affected. In addition, the supplier introduced a new visual error-prevention mechanism to limit concerns like this going forward.

BYD noted the matter does not affect the vehicle’s handling or pose a safety risk during driving.

The tech giant said owners can take affected vehicles to their local service center for a free inspection and professional wheel rim replacement. It’s also offering a replacement vehicle or compensation for transportation expenses.

Effective immediately, BYD said, the warranty on affected Great Tang vehicles will also be restarted.

The Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest Premium EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500).

Recent findings suggest that all versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries. While the base Premium model uses a 105.79 kWh battery, the Flagship EV trim uses a larger 130.15 kWh battery that delivers up to 590 miles (950 km) of CLTC range. It starts at 269,900 yuan ($40,000).

The Great Tang is huge, measuring 5,263 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,800 mm high, with a wheelbase of 3,130 mm.

In comparison, that’s bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 and Kia EV9. It’s closer in size to the Li Auto L9.

Based on a 1,000V architecture with BYD’s Flash Charging tech, the electric SUV can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. For a full recharge, or to go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

After launching in China, BYD executive vice president Stella Li said the flagship SUV will go on sale in Europe and other overseas markets by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

What Are Perpetual Futures? How Crypto's Most Popular Derivative Works

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, perpetual futures are the engine room of crypto trading.
  • It has been revealed that they aren't only for crypto, either.
  • This guide explains what futures are, what makes perpetual futures different, how funding rates and liquidations work, and what to know before trading them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, perpetual futures are the engine room of crypto trading. Centralized exchanges processed $85.3 trillion in perps trading volume in 2025 alone, according to CoinGecko's State of Crypto Perpetuals Report 2026, and the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) describes perps as the dominant form of crypto derivatives trading.

It has been revealed that they aren't only for crypto, either. Exchanges now offer perps on stocks, commodities and currencies, and Decrypt has become the first news publisher to offer perps trading, powered by Solana exchange Phoenix.

This guide explains what futures are, what makes perpetual futures different, how funding rates and liquidations work, and what to know before trading them.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

To understand perpetual futures, it helps to start with ordinary futures.

A futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell an asset at a set price on a set date in the future. Futures have been used for centuries: farmers used them to lock in prices for crops before harvest, and today they are traded on everything from oil and wheat to stock indexes and Bitcoin, on regulated exchanges such as CME.

Traders use futures for two main reasons. Hedgers use them to protect against price swings; an airline might buy oil futures to lock in fuel costs, for example. Speculators use them to bet on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

Traditional futures have an expiry date. When a contract expires, it settles, either by delivering the asset or, more often, by paying out the difference in cash. Traders who want to keep their position open must "roll" it into a latest contract, which can add costs and complexity.

Sources indicate that perpetual futures, often shortened to "perps" or "perpetual swaps," work like futures, but with one key difference: they never expire. Traders can hold a position for as long as they like, provided they have enough collateral to keep it open.

The idea was proposed by Yale economist Robert Shiller in a 1993 paper as a way to create markets for assets that are hard to trade directly. Perps took off in crypto. Crypto exchange BitMEX, widely credited with bringing perps to crypto, debuted a perpetual contract on Bitcoin in 2016. BitMEX itself closed in September 2026, but the product it pioneered has become the most traded instrument in crypto.

Sources indicate that A perpetual contract never actually involves owning the asset. Traders deposit collateral, or "margin," and their profit or loss depends entirely on how the price moves.

Sources indicate that when opening a perp position, a trader chooses a direction. Going long means betting the price will rise; going short means betting it will fall. Being able to short as easily as going long is one reason perps are popular: it lets traders profit from falling prices, or hedge assets they already own.

It has been revealed that perps are usually traded with leverage, which lets traders control a larger position than their collateral alone would allow. With 10x leverage, for example, $100 of margin controls a $1,000 position. If the asset's price rises 5%, the trader makes $50, a 50% return on their margin. But if it falls 5%, they lose $50, half of their margin.

Recent findings suggest that exchanges track two prices to manage this. The index price is the asset's price on spot markets, usually averaged across several exchanges. The mark price, based on the index and the perp market itself, is used to calculate profits and losses and to decide when positions must be closed. Using an averaged price makes it harder for a sudden spike on one exchange to trigger liquidations.

Because perps never expire, nothing forces their price to converge with the underlying asset, as traditional futures do at expiry. Instead, perps use a funding rate.

At regular intervals—most commonly every eight hours, though some platforms use shorter or longer schedules—traders on one side of the market pay traders on the other:.

Decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, for example, pays funding every hour, at one-eighth of the rate calculated for an eight-hour period, to stay consistent with centralized exchanges.

Funding payments go directly between traders, not to the exchange. For traders holding positions over long periods, these payments can add up, and they can either boost or erode returns.

According to recent reports, funding rates also offer a window into market sentiment. Strongly positive funding suggests traders are crowded into bullish bets, while negative funding demonstrates that bears are paying to stay short.

It has been revealed that rates for the same asset can also differ between exchanges. On November 19, 2026, Bitcoin's funding rate was 0.01% per eight hours on Hyperliquid, compared with 0.0037% on Binance, according to Hyperliquid's funding comparison tool.

Some traders aim to earn funding payments rather than bet on prices. In a "cash and carry" or basis trade, they buy an asset on the spot market and short the same amount through perps, collecting funding while their positions offset each other's price moves.

Leverage is a double-edged sword. Every perp position has a maintenance margin, the minimum collateral needed to keep it open. If losses push a trader's margin below that level, the exchange automatically closes the position, a process called liquidation. The trader typically loses most or all of the margin they put up.

It has been revealed that the higher the leverage, the smaller the price move needed to trigger a liquidation. At 50x leverage, a 2% move against a position can wipe it out.

Liquidations can also feed on each other. When prices fall sharply, liquidated longs are forced to sell, pushing prices lower and triggering further liquidations, a so-called liquidation cascade. On October 10, 2025, the crypto market saw its largest liquidation event on record, with more than $19 billion in leveraged positions wiped out in a single day.

To cover losses when positions can't be closed in time, exchanges typically keep an insurance fund. In extreme cases, some use auto-deleveraging, closing profitable positions on the other side of the market to keep the system solvent.

Crypto perps trade on two main types of venue.

Sources indicate that centralized exchanges, such as Binance, Bybit and OKX, run their own order books and hold consumers' funds. They account for the vast majority of perps trading: Binance alone held about a third of centralized perps volume in early 2026, according to CoinGecko. Many are unavailable to U.S. customers.

Industry observers note that decentralized exchanges let traders use perps through smart contracts, while keeping control of their funds. Some, such as Hyperliquid and Solana-based Phoenix, run order books onchain, matching buyers and sellers much like a traditional exchange. Others, such as GMX and Jupiter, let traders trade against a shared pool of liquidity provided by other users.

Decentralized perps are growing fast. Their trading volume jumped from $1.5 trillion in 2024 to $6.38 trillion in 2025, led by Hyperliquid, CoinGecko found. Decentralized exchanges' share of perps trading volume peaked at 13% in late 2025 before slipping to 10% in April 2026, while their share of open interest, the total value of open positions, reached 13.5%.

Sources indicate that in the U.S., perps developed largely on offshore exchanges, outside the reach of the CFTC, but that has started to change. In July 2025, Coinbase introduced CFTC-regulated "perpetual-style" futures for U.S. customers, with five-year expiries and up to 10x leverage. Two months later, CFTC-regulated exchange Bitnomial launched what it called the first U.S. perpetual futures, with 25-year terms and eight-hour funding. In May 2026, the CFTC approved a Bitcoin perpetual futures contract from prediction market Kalshi and set out a framework for listing more, and in June, Kraken rolled out perps to eligible U.S. customers through Bitnomial, which its parent tech giant had acquired.

It has been revealed that some of these contracts, including Kalshi's and Bitnomial's original design, have long but fixed terms of 25 years, so are not strictly perpetual. The regulator says perps can be offered on CFTC-registered exchanges under federal oversight, and has advised U.S. traders to avoid offshore venues.

Recent findings suggest that the shift has been contested. CME Group, the largest U.S. futures exchange, has sued the CFTC, arguing that perps are swaps rather than futures under U.S. law. The CFTC has nonetheless continued to approve more perps platforms, starting with Backpack.

Perps are now spreading beyond crypto. Exchanges have begun listing perps tracking stocks, stock indexes, commodities such as gold and oil, and currencies, giving traders around-the-clock exposure to markets that normally close in the evening and on weekends.

It has been revealed that those products carry the same mechanics, and the same risks, as crypto perps. They track an asset's price without giving traders ownership of the asset itself, so a perp on a firm's stock doesn't come with voting rights or dividends.

Perps can be useful tools for hedging and speculation, but they are among the riskiest products in crypto:.

Decrypt users can now trade perps directly alongside the news, through the Decrypt Money Account. The service is powered by Phoenix, a decentralized exchange on Solana, and lets users go long or short on crypto, stocks and commodities.

Availability varies by region, and as with any leveraged product, traders should only risk money they can afford to lose.

Home » Trendsetter News » Ripple ETF Investors Hold On, But XRP Buyers Go Missing.

XRP ETF assets fell 31.6% despite modest redemptions, suggesting a lack of fresh demand, not a buyer exodus.

Recent findings suggest that ripple’s XRP-linked ETF assets fell 31.6% from September 30 through the Friday cited in the video, compared with a 20.2% decline for Bitcoin funds. Yet redemptions remained modest.

Dana Love, PhD, a popular market analyst examining ETF flows and corporate filings, argues that missing buyers, not an investor stampede, help explain the XRP’s deeper slide this month.

The XRP coin traded at $0.967 this Friday morning, following a last Friday low of $0.89.

Dana Love’s central claim: Bitcoin-related selling is weighing on XRP, while demand from XRP funds and a closely watched treasury company has failed to provide much support.

According to the figures presented, cumulative net inflows into XRP ETFs slipped from $1.809 billion on October 29 to $1.789 billion on Monday. That leaves roughly 98.9% of cumulative net inflows intact, despite the sharp decline in fund assets.

In a recent development, but November through that Monday brought no positive daily net flows. “Nobody is running for the exits,” the analyst claims, “but nobody latest was walking in.”.

Bitcoin ETFs, meanwhile, recorded roughly $2.34 billion in November outflows through the same period. Monday’s $8 million inflow interrupted the selling, although the analyst cautions that one positive session does not establish a reversal.

Industry observers note that the distinction matters: limited XRP ETF redemptions do not establish that XRP holders across the entire market are refusing to sell. Nor does a decline in fund assets measure withdrawals alone; falling token prices also reduce those balances.

Dana Love also questions Evernorth, the XRP treasury manufacturer whose October 14 release said it would “accumulate and deploy” XRP into institutional strategies beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The video estimates that Evernorth had about $111 million in cash, including subsequent warrant proceeds, and says its shares still traded above estimated underlying asset value.

That could support further fundraising, although the firm had not confirmed additional purchases in the period discussed.

Sources indicate that silence is not proof of inactivity. The analyst explicitly acknowledges that Evernorth may be buying without announcing every transaction.

For investors, the useful distinction is between broader market relief and renewed XRP-specific market demand.

Sustained Bitcoin ETF inflows would suggest selling pressure is easing; XRP inflows arriving independently, or a disclosed Evernorth purchase, would offer stronger evidence that XRP has found buyers of its own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin reportedly became available at a massive discount on Kraken after a sharp dislocation in Kraken's dollar trading markets.

People reported being able to purchase BTC for as little as 24,250 CAD, equivalent to $16,900 at that time.

Apparently, the incident has only affected the BTC/CAD trading pair on the platform, although some people claim the disruption appeared across several CAD markets.

The cause the glitch is still unclear, while the reported transactions are yet to be verified.

The incident might have involved thin liquidity problem in Kraken's CAD order books.

Large sell orders reportedly overwhelmed available buy orders, leaving insufficient demand to absorb the selling pressure.

According to some accounts, at one point about 20 BTC was being sold every 15 minutes, causing the imbalance to push BTC price against CAD further down.

Industry observers note that one such transaction resulted in BTC price at around C$24,250, or $16,900. Compared with Bitcoin trading between $57,000-$58,000, the discount amounted to a staggering 71%. Other people reported BTC briefly trading around $27,000.

Sources indicate that kraken's status page continued to show its systems as operational during the incident. No official explanation from the exchange was available at the time of writing.

Sources indicate that the reported dislocation highlights the risks associated with trading in markets with limited liquidity. When an order book lacks sufficient buy-side depth, even relatively large sell orders can cause prices to move sharply away from the broader market.

On Friday, Bitcoin price dropped below $60,000. At some point, it fell 5.10% to $55,830, the lowest level since September 2024.

Sources indicate that liquidations on crypto exchanges reached $1.57 billion over 24 hours on Nov. 20.

According to CoinGlass, 265,525 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of the total.

Bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions. Ethereum (ETH) fell below $1,700 on Nov. 20, and ETH traders saw $331.08 million in liquidations.

Binance accounted for 45.8% of all liquidations, and the largest single order was also on Binance: an $11.98 million ETH/USDT long position that was liquidated at $1,638.78.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coinbase wants a piece of the prediction markets action, with the exchange reportedly planning a launch next year.
  • Right now, they don’t run their own; they borrow them.
  • Citing sources close to the matter, a Bloomberg report claimed that Coinbase wants to roll out its own event contracts in the U.S in H1 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinbase wants a piece of the prediction markets action, with the exchange reportedly planning a launch next year.

Right now, they don’t run their own; they borrow them. Owners trade event contracts on the exchange through a Kalshi partnership. That could change next year though.

Citing sources close to the matter, a Bloomberg report claimed that Coinbase wants to roll out its own event contracts in the U.S in H1 2027. It would be open to both retail and institutional traders.

But why bother? For starters, Coinbase gets to decide what launches and when. Next, it keeps a bigger share of the trading fees.

Recent findings suggest that there’s real money at stake here. In Q3 2026, Coinbase’s prediction markets business was already on track to bring in over $200 million a year. If you think about it, this isn’t an overnight decision. In the run up to it all, Coinbase announced that it was buying prediction market startup The Clearing Manufacturer in December 2025.

Then, in September this year, the CFTC gave the green light for its own clearing house.

In a recent development, all that being stated, nothing’s set in stone. However, the pieces are clearly falling into place.

Crypto trading may have slowed down, but prediction markets have kept themselves out of the bleeding.

According to recent reports, since launch, revenue from the business has grown by 82% QoQ on average. In Q3 alone, daily traders went up by over 60%, compared to the quarter before.

CFO Alesia Haas summed up the appeal pretty neatly. She noted,.

Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility….

A big deal for an exchange that lives and dies by market cycles.

On the earnings call, Haas also mentioned that the upcoming clearing house would let Coinbase run its own contracts and earn more from them.

Worth pointing out, however, that Kalshi isn’t being cut out as partner contracts will stay on the platform.

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (945 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ambcrypto ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Best Hyperliquid trading bots: AI agents and bots compared

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (945 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, hyperliquid has become one of the busiest venues for crypto perpetual futures, and a long list of tools now automate trading on it.
  • According to recent reports, most Hyperliquid tools connect through an API wallet, which Hyperliquid also calls an agent wallet.
  • According to recent reports, many tools charge through a builder fee, a small fee added to each filled order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hyperliquid has become one of the busiest venues for crypto perpetual futures, and a long list of tools now automate trading on it. They differ less in what they promise than in two practical questions: who decides the trades, and what the tool is allowed to do with your account. This guide compares the main Hyperliquid trading bots and AI trading agents in 2026, plus Hyperliquid’s vaults, against those questions. Each tool was compared on who decides the trades, what its key can do with your account, and what evidence of performance exists, using each provider’s own documentation in October 2026.

According to recent reports, most Hyperliquid tools connect through an API wallet, which Hyperliquid also calls an agent wallet. The account owner approves a separate key that can sign orders for the account but cannot withdraw or transfer funds. These approvals expire, and approving a new wallet under the same name replaces the old one. Some tools also recommend a sub-account, which keeps the bot’s balances and positions separate. The assets stay in the user’s own Hyperliquid account throughout, which is why most Hyperliquid bots can fairly be called non-custodial.

According to recent reports, many tools charge through a builder fee, a small fee added to each filled order. It applies only after the user approves a maximum fee from the main wallet, and Hyperliquid caps it at 0.1% on perpetuals.

Sources indicate that tools are grouped by who supplies the trading logic: a managed model first, then signal execution, rule-based bots and open-source software (3Commas sits with the rule-based bots). Vaults come last because they replace a bot rather than run one. Hyperliquid’s own trading and funding fees apply to every option.

AlphaNet is built for Hyperliquid and supplies the trading logic itself. Users pick one of its deep learning strategies for crypto perpetual futures and an allocation, and the model decides when to enter and exit each trade. It connects the way the exchange intends: the user approves an agent wallet that can place and cancel orders but cannot withdraw or transfer, and trades run from the user’s own account. New deployments allow leverage up to 3× account equity. On cost, AlphaNet’s Hyperliquid trading bot charges no platform fee during the current promotional period, compared with builder fees of 0.035–0.1% per fill on several bots below; Hyperliquid’s protocol fees still apply, and a dynamic trading fee applies afterwards.

Sources indicate that A newer group of AI agent projects on Hyperliquid connect language models to an API wallet and let them place trades. They are mostly early. In the first season of Alpha Arena, a short real-money competition on Hyperliquid, four of the six language models that took part finished with losses and two with gains.

Recent findings suggest that wunderTrading is built for traders whose strategy already exists as TradingView alerts or external signals. It turns those alerts into Hyperliquid orders and also offers DCA and grid bots, charging a 0.035% builder fee with no separate subscription.

goodcryptoX is a no-code app for grid, DCA, trailing, and TradingView bots on iOS, Android, and the web. Gainium covers similar bot types and adds backtesting and paper trading, with a choice between a free mode that adds a builder fee and paid plans that do not. Bitsgap brings its hosted grid and DCA bots to Hyperliquid alongside the centralised exchanges it already supports, and 3Commas, one of the most widely used bot platforms, lists Hyperliquid among its supported exchanges for spot and futures. With all of them, the bot executes your logic; the tool does not supply a trading edge.

According to recent reports, hummingbot has Hyperliquid spot and perpetual connectors and includes market-making scripts and arbitrage, TWAP, and grid executors. The self-run client charges no builder fee. It accepts either an API wallet or the main wallet’s private key; the second gives the software full control of the account, so the API wallet is the safer choice.

Recent findings suggest that rule-based bots have no platform-level record, because results depend on each user’s settings. Vaults are the most transparent option: every vault’s history is on-chain and visible in Hyperliquid’s app. Managed strategy platforms sit in between. AlphaNet publishes a running record of each strategy since its start date, and because trades run from people’ own accounts, each user’s fills are on-chain and can be checked against it.

Sources indicate that instead of connecting a tool to your own account, you deposit into a vault that a leader trades. The protocol’s own vault, HLP, provides liquidity, performs liquidations, and earns a share of fees. User-run vaults follow individual strategies. Leaders take 10% of profits and must keep at least 5% of the vault, and deposits are locked for one day (four days for HLP).

Recent findings suggest that the choice comes down to the two questions this guide started with. First, decide who you want making the trades: your own rules, a signal you already trust, a trained model, or a vault leader. Then check what the tool is allowed to do with your account. On Hyperliquid, most tools need only an agent wallet that can trade but not withdraw, so there is rarely a reason to hand over a main wallet key or move funds into someone else’s control.

Two further checks are worth making before committing real capital. The first is cost per fill: builder fees on top of Hyperliquid’s own fees can add up. The second is the record: a vault’s history is on-chain, a managed strategy should publish a live one, and a rule-based bot has none until you build your own.

In a recent development, crypto exchange Binance has issued a "one-letter" security warning to crypto users, urging them to carefully check website addresses before logging into their accounts. According to Binance, a fake site can be just one letter off.

A post on X by the crypto exchange pointed out that a small difference in a website URL, sometimes just one letter, can lead people to visit fake websites impersonating legitimate platforms.

"Sometimes the biggest red flag is just one letter," Binance wrote.

The exchange advised owners to double-check URLs before entering their login credentials. It also encouraged anyone uncertain about a website's authenticity to use Binance's official verification tool to confirm whether the URL belongs to the platform.

The Binance Verify platform allows crypto consumers to stay safe from scammers, as they can enter a URL, email address, phone number, Telegram account, or social media account to check if the source is verified and officially from Binance.

It has been revealed that impersonation scams are quietly growing across the crypto space, with one of the most troubling tactics seen being the deepfake: lifelike, AI-generated impersonations of crypto executives and employees soliciting money on video calls that look and sound real enough to make anyone hesitate. The personas are fabricated, but the sophistication is genuine.

Every day, people are contacted by impersonators using the names, likenesses, and even job titles of crypto personnel, including Binance staff, to solicit investments or financial transactions via WhatsApp, Telegram, and other channels.

Binance stated that scammers prey on people's growing interest in investing and digital finance and on their trust, often masquerading as its employees or executives to exploit its credibility.

According to recent reports, with advances in AI and deepfake technology, they can create personas that look and sound real. Crypto users are therefore urged to beware of unsolicited advice or "special opportunities" and to refrain from clicking on unknown links or URLs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solana’s core developer, Anza, has unveiled its 2027 roadmap.

Sources indicate that structurally, the roadmap focuses on making Solana faster, more efficient, and capable of handling more activity. The network aims to double its compute capacity and cut the compute units needed for token account transactions by 80%.

It also plans to increase the number of accounts supported in each transaction from 64 to 96 and make it easier to run models fully on-chain.

Recent findings suggest that naturally, the question becomes whether Solana is preparing for its next growth phase. Interestingly, the previous major network upgrade was also performed by Anza.

This upgrade, called Alpenglow, brought down Solana’s finality time to 150ms from 12.8 seconds, making the network significantly faster.

According to recent reports, the result? As the chart above shows, Solana processed over 10 billion transactions in October, keeping monthly activity above that level. However, more than halfway through November, the network has recorded just over 2 billion transactions.

That’s 5x lower than October’s total, suggesting that the recent spike in activity may be losing steam. Given this, it might be too early to expect any bull run in 2027.

In fact, SOL is currently down 20% in October, which indicates that the market hasn’t seen increased demand from improving fundamentals just yet.

So, what does it say about the recent “Anthropic-driven” momentum on Solana [SOL]?

SPCX was first to demonstrate how major IPOs can bring fresh trading activity to Solana.

The launch of SpaceX’s tokenized stock, SPCX, on Solana on the 12th of June brought significant activity to the network.

The token recorded $108 million in 24-hour on-chain trading volume shortly after launch and crossed 10,000 holders within six days, with cumulative trading volume exceeding $350 million.

Notably, a similar trend has emerged following the ANT IPO launch. As the chart below reveals, Anthropic’s ANT has generated over $29 million in trading volume on Solana since launch across three issuers. Backpack’s token alone accounted for $26.8 million, or nearly 92% of the total.

This highlights how major IPO releases are bringing fresh trading activity to Solana.

Adding to this, DeFiLlama data indicates that Solana’s stablecoin market cap has risen nearly 3% in the past 24 hours, pointing to a fresh liquidity inflow after months of weakness.

However, the bigger picture remains mixed.

Despite the rise in on-chain activity and liquidity, SOL is still trading around $70. This suggests that the recent activity has yet to translate into stronger buying pressure.

For Solana’s 2027 roadmap to support a longer-term recovery, the network will therefore need to sustain this growth beyond short-term activity.

Anza’s 2027 roadmap aims to improve Solana’s speed, capacity, and overall network efficiency.

SPCX and ANT have boosted on-chain trading activity, but SOL’s price weakness suggests that stronger demand is still missing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia became the first non-European brand to score a hat trick at the 2026 Golden Steering Wheel Awards, Germany’s most prestigious auto awards.

The Korean automaker won a triple crown at the 2026 Golden Steering Wheel Awards, with the EV2, K4 Sportswagon, and EV5 taking first in their class.

This is the first time a non-European brand has won three Golden Steering Wheel Awards in a single year in the prestigious award’s 50-year history.

It has been revealed that the award is organized by AUTO BILD and BILD am SONNTAG with 90 upcoming models nominated this year. Readers chose 27 finalists, three in each of the nine classes, which were then tested by a panel of celebrities and auto experts.

Industry observers note that the judges tested the vehicles at the DEKRA-Lausitzring racetrack. Vehicles were judged on handling, comfort, ease of use, quality, and everyday practicality, as well as the sustainability and value they offer.

Kia won across three very different categories with the fully electric EV2 and EV5, alongside the gas-powered K4 Sportswagon.

The EV2, Kia’s entry-level electric SUV, won the award for the “Best Car Under €30,000.” Developed specifically for Europe, the compact EV is only 4.06 meters long, but offers up to 403 liters of cargo space.

It also offers a WLTP driving range of up to 453 km (281 miles), which is among the longest in its class.

Recent findings suggest that kia’s EV5 beat out the Audi Q3 and Cupra Formentor VZ5 in the compact SUV category. Debuted in December, the EV5 is about the size of the Sportage.

It has been revealed that it’s available with front- and all-wheel-drive powertrains and offers a range of over 550 km (341 miles). Depending on the configuration, the EV5 can tow up to 1,800 kg (about 4,000 lbs).

Lastly, the Kia K4 Sportswagon, launched in May, outperformed the fresh Volkswagen ID.3 Neo and Cupra Born in the compact class.

In Europe, Kia offers a full lineup of all-electric vehicles, from the entry-level EV2 to the EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, three-row EV9, and PV5 van.

Sadly, Kia has no aims to sell the EV2 or EV5 in the US, but its popular EV3 (see our review) is now available. In 2024, the Kia EV3 won the Golden Steering Wheel award for “Best Car under €40,000.”.

It has been revealed that the 2027 Kia EV3 starts at $29,890, making it among the most affordable EVs in the US. It’s available in five trims and two battery packs.

The base Kia EV3 Light has a 58.3 kWh battery that provides up to 221 miles of range, while the Wind, Land, GT-Line, and GT use an 81.4 kWh battery for up to 321 miles of range.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the US order barring covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC takes effect Dec.
  • MEXC can keep matching buy and sell orders in the markets it still serves, while one of the world's largest exchanges has already told traders it will restrict what they can move between the two.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that that's what Binance told customers to expect while it reviews deposits from MEXC. Try to move money the other way, and Binance claims it'll refuse to send it in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that the US order barring covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC takes effect Dec. 10, but Binance unveiled its policy a month earlier and cited the Treasury's finding.

MEXC can keep matching buy and sell orders in the markets it still serves, while one of the world's largest exchanges has already told traders it will restrict what they can move between the two.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 6, the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) found that MEXC was a foreign financial institution of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.

The agency acted under Section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, and its order in the Federal Register prohibits transfers to and from MEXC through covered US financial institutions.

The prohibition has no scheduled end and covers MEXC's foreign operations and successor entities. It reaches crypto as well as conventional money, and FinCEN names Bitcoin explicitly.

Foreign financial firms can make dollar payments through banks that hold accounts with US banks, an arrangement known as correspondent banking.

Sources indicate that finCEN considered restricting those accounts but concluded that doing so would leave other kinds of transfers untouched. Instead, it chose to prohibit transfers that pass through a covered institution, even when MEXC has no account with the institution handling the payment.

Exchanges and payment providers outside that group may adopt their own restrictions, but those policies require separate confirmation.

FinCEN estimates that MEXC handled at least $16.7 billion in likely illicit activity in the five years through May 2026. The agency's figures include about $129 million it notes MEXC directly facilitated with Garantex after the Russian crypto exchange was sanctioned, and about $4.1 million involving its successor, Grinex, after it too was sanctioned.

Industry observers note that finCEN also cites transfers linked to Iran and North Korea, along with proceeds from cybercrime. The agency acknowledges that legitimate customers use MEXC and claims the financial risks it identified warrant restricting transfers involving the exchange itself.

According to recent reports, in its Nov. 7 public response, MEXC noted it was operating normally, and customer assets remained secure. It said it had opened an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls and intended to engage with regulators.

Reports noted net outflows from tracked MEXC wallets after the announcement.

Binance can refuse to send a withdrawal because it controls the account the money would leave.

Yet, when crypto comes from another platform, the network can process the transaction without asking the recipient's permission.

FinCEN acknowledges that limitation in the order, and Binance's notice shows what the exchange can do once the funds arrive: it can withhold credit while it reviews the transfer and potentially restrict or close the customer's Binance account.

Any funds left at MEXC stay in that account unless the customer moves them separately.

Sources indicate that an on-chain confirmation and exchange-account credit are separate events. Binance states deposits from MEXC entities are withheld for review, while outgoing requests are declined.

Blockchain settlement does not force a receiving exchange to credit a customer balance.

Recent findings suggest that binance describes platform policy, not a documented individual incident. FinCEN binds covered US financial institutions. A confirmed blockchain transaction does not guarantee immediate account credit; account restrictions are possible, not certain.

In a recent development, based on the Binance notice published November 10, 2026, and the FinCEN order published November 10 with a December 10 effective date. Inbound path is illustrative; no verified individual customer transfer is claimed.

Binance describes platform policy, not a documented individual incident. FinCEN binds covered US financial institutions. A confirmed blockchain transaction does not guarantee immediate account credit; account restrictions are possible, not certain.

The business risk for exchanges becomes more serious if customers and professional market makers, the firms that keep buy and sell orders available, lose more ways to fund their accounts or move out the proceeds.

Moving balances between exchanges is part of how those firms keep money available where they need it.

Sources indicate that MEXC claims changes at third-party issuers ended its Asia-Pacific card program on Nov. 11 and its Global Card on Nov. 18.

According to recent reports, global Card customers can no longer use their cards for purchases. MEXC says it will credit balances left on the cards to customers' spot accounts within three business days of a Nov. 21 snapshot.

That would leave customers with an exchange balance rather than a working payment card, because spending it with a card requires an issuer.

In France, MEXC had announced its wind-down in October, before the Treasury acted. Its schedule for French accounts stopped euro deposits and withdrawals on Nov. 18, while crypto withdrawals remain available until March 5, 2027.

According to recent reports, trading restrictions begin in batches, and French accounts enter withdrawal-only mode on Jan. 25.

On Nov. 20, DefiLlama displayed more than $1 billion in MEXC spot trading over 24 hours. That figure measures trading across the platform, including customers outside France, and says little about whether an individual French account can accept deposits, place newly introduced orders, or withdraw its remaining funds.

After Dec. 10, the practical reach of FinCEN's order will depend partly on which banks and exchanges handle a trader's money and which restrictions those firms apply.

It has been revealed that binance has already told customers how it intends to handle MEXC transfers. Other firms may take different approaches, which traders will discover when they try to withdraw a balance, deposit it somewhere else, or spend it through a payment service.

This transactions are not impulsive moves but part of a carefully planned 10-year strategy. Over the past decade, a total of 49,751 ETH has been sent from these addresses to exchanges.

The average selling price was a modest $658 by today's standards, although it’s worth noting that these coins were originally acquired in the project's early days, when ETH was worth less than a dollar.

Ethereum is at the moment going through one of its most challenging times in recent memory. Investor sentiment is still low, network activity has dispersed throughout Layer-2 solutions.

In addition to that, Ethereum has spent most of 2026 underperforming many rival ecosystems.

Earlier this year, Hsiao-Wei Wang has stepped down from the roles of co-executive director and board member of the Ethereum Foundation. In February, fellow co-Executive Director Tomasz Stańczak also stepped down.

Ethereum foundation has been selling ETH in 2026 during steep price movements, both up and down. For instance, BitMine acquired 10,000 ETH at an average price of $2,292 this June.

A similar sale one week earlier, where another 10,000 ETH was sold at $2,387 per coin.

On Friday, Bitcoin price dropped below $60,000. At some point, it fell 5.10% to $55,830, the lowest level since September 2024.

Industry observers note that liquidations on crypto exchanges reached $1.57 billion over 24 hours on Nov. 20. According to CoinGlass, 265,525 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of the total.

Bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions.

#64473. Tech Report: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam delay reveals a troubling pattern behind its biggest network upgrades

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (876 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cryptoslate ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam delay reveals a troubling pattern behind its biggest network upgrades

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.
  • 20, Ethereum Foundation researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the upgrade, which the foundation had targeted for the first half of 2026, cannot reach mainnet before mid-January 2027, after delays disrupted its testing schedule.
  • In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached upcoming highs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 20, Ethereum Foundation researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the upgrade, which the foundation had targeted for the first half of 2026, cannot reach mainnet before mid-January 2027, after delays disrupted its testing schedule.

In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached upcoming highs.

“Nobody did a bad job, but I think we fooled ourselves, twice.”.

His findings show that Glamsterdam was assigned the shortest development timeline in years despite being Ethereum's most ambitious upgrade by several measures.

According to Wahrstätter, monthly contributions to Ethereum's technical specifications have increased between twofold and 3.5-fold since 2024, reflecting a substantial acceleration in development activity.

The improvement has extended to testing. Glamsterdam completed 12 development networks, or devnets, in 160 days, compared with seven devnets over 285 days for Pectra, an earlier Ethereum upgrade.

However, Wahrstätter argued that the acceleration has created another problem: developers can now produce specifications, code and tests faster than their colleagues can review them and understand their implications.

It has been revealed that that challenge has become more pronounced with Glamsterdam's unprecedented size. The upgrade contains approximately 6,080 lines of execution-layer specifications, compared with 2,318 for Prague, the previous record.

In a separate count of proposal specifications, Wahrstätter put two of Glamsterdam's most crucial changes, enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS) and block-level access lists (BALs), at approximately 11,900 and 9,300 lines, respectively. The other 16 proposals collectively represent about 3,600 lines.

The complexity is also reflected in EIP-8037, a proposal that changes how Ethereum charges for creating fresh blockchain state. Although its specifications contain roughly 1,700 lines, the proposal requires approximately 30,000 lines of tests, more than any other proposal included in the upgrade.

Together, this illustrates why faster code production has failed to produce a corresponding acceleration in network upgrades.

Sources indicate that indeed, Wahrstätter's historical analysis showed that every Ethereum upgrade since Dencun has taken more than 400 days from finalizing its scope to reaching mainnet. For context, the three most recent upgrades took between 433 and 475 days, even though their technical scope was smaller than Glamsterdam's.

Despite that record, Glamsterdam was given a development target of just 320 days, substantially shorter than the timelines achieved by previous upgrades.

Industry observers note that wahrstätter found that virtually every Ethereum upgrade with an announced target had missed its deadline. Fusaka was the exception, but only after developers removed Ethereum Object Format (EOF), a major component originally planned for inclusion.

Pectra similarly required developers to divide its original scope across separate upgrades.

According to recent reports, glamsterdam took a different approach. Developers kept adding proposals to successive testing environments while work on its two main components, ePBS and BALs, continued.

Unlike earlier upgrades, the team made no comparable reduction in scope to protect its development timeline.

Consequently, Glamsterdam reached public testing before its specifications had stabilized, creating additional work at a stage when developers would ordinarily be preparing for deployment.

Wahrstätter's analysis showed that Ethereum upgrades between Altair and Deneb recorded no specification changes after their first public testnet.

Pectra recorded two changes, while Fusaka recorded one. Glamsterdam registered 10 in just six weeks.

The difference also appeared in client development. Work on Pectra declined substantially after public testing began, whereas Glamsterdam-related activity increased 34% following its Sepolia activation, alongside a 25% rise in client commits.

Those late changes became particularly consequential after security researchers identified problems involving EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, which alter how Ethereum charges for certain operations.

In a recent development, the proposals could disrupt assumptions embedded in existing smart contracts, prompting developers to postpone Glamsterdam's Oct. 26 activation on the Hoodi testnet.

The setback has pushed Glamsterdam's expected interval between its first public testnet and mainnet activation beyond 100 days, compared with the 4- to 10-week window typical of previous upgrades, according to Wahrstätter.

Industry observers note that during their Nov. 19 meeting, Ethereum developers tentatively targeted Dec. 16 or 17 for Hoodi testing, with mid-January 2027 emerging as the earliest possible mainnet date if the specification stays unchanged.

Wahrstätter argued that preventing further delays would require developers to base release targets on historical performance and set firm deadlines for dropping unfinished features and completing specifications before public testing begins.

He also questioned treating successful devnet deployments as evidence that proposals were sufficiently mature for inclusion in an upgrade. He said:.

“I'm sure we can ship faster, but for that, we must ship smaller.”.

Recent findings suggest that the next decision comes Nov. 26, when Ethereum's core developers are expected to determine whether Glamsterdam can proceed with its proposed December Hoodi activation.

A further postponement would place additional pressure on a release schedule that has already extended well beyond its original target.

Both versions measure 5,080 mm long, 1,960 mm wide, and 1,495 mm high, with a 2,960 mm wheelbase, which is slightly longer than the Toyota Camry.

Don’t let the price fool you, however, the vehicle is packed with BYD’s latest breakthrough technology.

The fresh Seal 07 EV uses a 76.7 kWh second-generation BYD Blade LFP battery that provides a CLTC range of up to 481 miles (775 km).

Thanks to the second-gen Blade Batteries and BYD’s Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 70% in just five minutes. A full recharge, or going from 10% to 97%, takes just nine minutes.

The Seal 07 is also BYD’s first vehicle to debut with its fresh Disus-M Intelligent Magnetorheological Body Control System.

Recent findings suggest that the setup features a front double-wishbone suspension and an enhanced rear five-link suspension. It works alongside BYD’s road-surface sensors that use LiDAR, plus its iTAC 2.0 Intelligent Torque Adaptation System.

Zhang Zhuo, the general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, offered a better look at how the system works in real life in the video shown above.

In a recent development, BYD said the system provides ultra-fast response times down to the millisecond. The advanced suspension system adjusts damping force across a wide range of 100 to 10,000 Nm.

It has been revealed that it’s equipped on the all-electric Flagship Seal 07 variant, while lower-priced versions have the Disus-C intelligent body control system. The top-spec EV model with the Disus-M setup starts at 172,900 yuan ($26,000). Still, not too bad for what you get.

Inside, the newly introduced Seal 07 adopts BYD’s new interior design, including a 15.6″ floating center infotainment screen, a 10.25″ instrument cluster, and two rear passenger entertainment screens.

BYD added a few premium extras, including a built-in 6.8L smart refrigerator, zero gravity seats, and driver headrest audio.

Quite impressive for sure. What's more impressive is that GM/Cadillac first offered magnetic ride control back in 2002 (a full 24 years ago!!). It may not have been quite as advanced as this system in 2026, but still one of the most advanced suspension systems offered to date for a line of vehicles.

I really want this car!! I truly hope BYD will be able to sell this in the USA soon.

The Seal 07 also debuts BYD’s Smart Ecosystem 2.0, including “Diva,” a smartwatch that lets drivers interact with the vehicle and manage functions remotely.

Higher-priced versions are available with BYD’s God’s Eye B intelligent driving system, which includes a roof-mounted LiDAR. The setup provides safety and convenience features like Navigation on Autopilot in the city and on highways, plus full-scenario intelligent parking.

For a limited time, BYD is offering a “Super trade-in price” special, starting at 145,900 yuan ($22,000) for the new Seal 07 EV and 135,900 yuan ($20,500) for the PHEV version.
